qualifying_findings.source_title: Copilot code review: API support and new default effort level
qualifying_findings.date_qualification: Visible source date is inside the cutoff window.
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: GitHub says Copilot code review can now be requested through REST and GraphQL APIs, callers can set review effort per request, and Balanced is now the default effort level for Copilot code review unless Lite was explicitly selected.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: AI review is becoming workflow-triggerable infrastructure rather than only an interactive PR action. Local practice should track API-triggered review provenance, effort-level defaults, review-cost policy, and whether repository or organization defaults changed the expected review depth.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Route broad product details upstream; locally, capture review-effort configuration, API-trigger evidence, and governance controls for automated AI review requests.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: During ingest, consider whether repository-configured AI code review and code-review eval leaves should mention API-triggered review requests and effort defaults.

qualifying_findings.source_title: Dynamic workflows in Copilot CLI and the Copilot app
qualifying_findings.date_qualification: Visible source date is inside the cutoff window.
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: GitHub describes dynamic workflows as code-defined orchestrations in Copilot CLI, the Copilot app, and the Copilot SDK that can combine commands, tools, services, parallel tasks, subagent verification, structured results, user input, checkpoints, and resume behavior.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Reusable agent workflows are moving toward reviewable program artifacts with explicit checkpoints and structured handoffs. Local practice should treat workflow definitions as governed source artifacts with validation, permission boundaries, and audit evidence rather than as one-off prompts.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Keep product coverage upstream; locally, capture reusable workflow-as-code patterns, checkpoint review, structured result propagation, and subagent verification gates.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Potential ingest destinations include declarative agent workflow artifacts, agent control flow selection, and subagent coordination.

qualifying_findings.source_title: GitHub Copilot in VS Code, September 2026 releases
qualifying_findings.date_qualification: Visible source date is inside the cutoff window.
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: GitHub summarizes September VS Code agent updates: recurring automations, agent merge handling review feedback and failed checks, PR creation from agent sessions, hierarchical related-session navigation, completed-session cleanup, attention badges, Dev Container sessions, workspace attachment for chats, and continuing Codex work from ChatGPT in VS Code.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Agent work surfaces are converging around session lifecycle management, status attention, environment selection, PR packaging, and cross-app continuity. Local practice should preserve session provenance and avoid treating cross-surface continuation as context-free work.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Capture lifecycle and handoff practice locally; route broad product and availability details upstream.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Consider ingest into persistent agent workspaces, supervised cross-environment handoffs, shared channel agent sessions, and agent environment readiness.

qualifying_findings.source_title: GitHub Copilot can now interact with desktop apps with computer use
qualifying_findings.date_qualification: Visible source date is inside the cutoff window.
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: GitHub says computer use is in public preview for Copilot CLI and the Copilot app on macOS and Windows. Copilot can read accessible app content and visual context, click controls, enter text, press keys, scroll, drag, and navigate GUI workflows. The post says users approve app control, can review or reset always-allowed apps, macOS requires Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions, and managed settings can disable the feature.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Desktop automation expands agent authority beyond repository files and command-line tools into GUI applications. Local practice needs explicit outcome descriptions, app allowlists, permission review, screen-recording privacy boundaries, reset paths, and organization policy controls before desktop control is treated as normal development workflow.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Route broad feature coverage upstream; locally, capture cross-environment handoff, app-control approval evidence, and privacy constraints.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Potential ingest targets include supervised cross-environment handoffs, browser-agent runtime boundaries, execution-edge authorization, and human-agent approval boundaries.

qualifying_findings.source_title: Test-First Development with Codex: Using TDD as the Agent Feedback Loop
qualifying_findings.date_qualification: Visible update date is inside the cutoff window.
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: The article frames tests as the objective feedback interface for autonomous coding agents, recommends writing failing tests before dispatch, warns that agents may weaken tests unless guarded, and shows AGENTS.md-style testing protocols plus automatic test-loop hooks.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: It reinforces local TDD guidance that tests should encode intent before agent implementation and that guardrails must protect tests from being edited merely to satisfy a completion objective.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Local wiki should keep the practice lens: failing tests as acceptance signals, anti-test-weakening rules, and hook-supported regression loops.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: During ingest, compare with existing ai-assisted-tdd and verification loops leaves to avoid duplicating already-processed TDD guidance.

qualifying_findings.source_title: Adversarial Review: Why Structured Disagreement Beats Consensus in Agentic Code Review
qualifying_findings.date_qualification: Visible update date is inside the cutoff window.
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: The article describes a three-role adversarial review protocol with a main agent, reviewer, and critic. It emphasizes evidence-grounded disagreement categories, capped inner-loop convergence, outer-loop edits only after converged review issues, budget accounting, and writable-scope constraints.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: It provides a concrete practice pattern for avoiding false consensus in AI review: critic roles should require code evidence or force retraction, and edit authority should be gated on converged, evidence-backed findings.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Route benchmark and product background upstream; locally, capture the role-separated review protocol, evidence obligation, convergence gate, budget cap, and scope-control practice.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Potential ingest destinations include multi-reviewer AI code review, code-review evals and rubrics, subagent coordination, and agent lifecycle hooks.

qualifying_findings.visible_date: October 2, 2026 afternoon edition and October 2, 2026 morning edition
qualifying_findings.date_qualification: Visible briefing dates are inside the cutoff window; treated as a secondary briefing, not authoritative product documentation.
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: The briefing states that October 1 agent-harness updates included plugin-level tool-call paths, Pi 1.0 plus an experimental durable runtime, GitHub Copilot desktop-app control, and a continuing gap where builders assemble their own permission layer. It also highlights recent analysis about crash recovery, local daemon defaults, plugin permission behavior, and MCP allowlists.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The secondary signal is not a product source, but it usefully clusters a practice trend: agent harness capability is advancing faster than uniform permission, durability, and daemon-governance patterns. Local practice should keep permission layers, crash recovery, plugin voting, and daemon exposure as explicit acceptance criteria.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Do not duplicate entity updates; retain the local governance implication that permission, crash recovery, local daemon exposure, and plugin authority must be tested as harness controls.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Use only as supporting context during ingest; verify each product-specific claim against primary sources before durable synthesis.
